clue.text: See 27
Sons pick greatly amusing person

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
the pick of something is its cream, the best part

explanation.surface: Someone choosing boys for a team turns out to be hilarious company.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a very funny person is called a scream, someone who makes everyone laugh.

clue.text: Lookalike's campanologist no longer with us

parts.note: a euphemism for dead
a campanologist rings church bells, so is a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A double for a bell-ringer who has passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Lookalike is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks exactly like another person is an idiomatic double, a dead ringer.

clue.text: Horse's joint that's broken itself

indicators.note: broken signals the word itself is smashed and its letters put back together differently

explanation.surface: A horse's joint that has fractured all on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' looks like a mere pronoun but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The stifle is the joint in a horse's hind leg corresponding to the human knee.

clue.text: Some local cut taxes in city once

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the local tax burden is being reduced in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the definition: the city was 'once' so named, as Kolkata is now officially called.
explanation.definitionFit: Kolkata in India was formerly known in English by this older name.

clue.text: Caught important little bird

indicators.note: caught means caught by the ear, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: important is key, and little is wee in Scottish usage, together said as key-wee

explanation.surface: A small bird of some importance has been captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' wants to be the cricket abbreviation C, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless national bird of New Zealand is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Changing sound to captivate rising artist

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a sound plan is viable, workable

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A shifting noise that enthrals an up-and-coming painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something variable is liable to change, so the adjective matches changing in sense.

clue.text: Motorway bus, leaving darkness, comes to marsh

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: leaving means the word bus departs from inside the larger word

parts.note: Erebus is the Greek personification of primeval darkness
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach on the motorway emerges from the dark into wetland.
explanation.walkthrough: Erebus, the god of darkness in Greek myth, loses BUS to leave ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pool, and dictionaries also give it as a marshy fen.

clue.text: Revolutionary star playing with men in big band

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel celebrity performs alongside the musicians of a large band.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers come last in the clue but OR heads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony group of many players is a large ensemble, a big band in a loose sense.

clue.text: Single male to get on creates public persona

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: An unmarried man getting older builds a public reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's image is the impression presented to the world, their outward persona.

clue.text: Give up being ridiculously idle after years

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the abbreviation
ridiculously says the word idle is treated absurdly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders after years of absurd laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender or relinquish, giving something up.

clue.text: Stat showing lack of thought about minutes is rejected

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a facile remark is superficial, showing little thought

indicators.note: rejected means the pair is turned back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A statistic revealing thoughtlessness about minutes gets thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stat' looks like a statistic, but it is short for photostat, a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A photostat, shortened to stat, is a photocopy, an exact reproduction of a document.

clue.text: Puzzling polemic put together

indicators.note: puzzling suggests the letters are muddled up and must be worked out

explanation.surface: A baffling diatribe that has been assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to gather material and assemble it into one collection.

clue.text: Tory holds Liberal ultimately responsible for hacked phone

indicators.note: holds means the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Conservative blames a Liberal for a phone-hacking scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone reprogrammed to share another's identity is called a cloned handset.

clue.text: See 23
First drink, then second for each among themselves?

parts.note: one is the first number
after one drink you order another, a second

explanation.surface: A first drink, then a second for everybody among the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes reciprocal action, each member doing something to the others.

clue.text: Dean flayed by cardinal and devoured

indicators.note: flayed means skinned, so the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: ten is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A clergyman skinned by a senior churchman and consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman beside the dean, but it means a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten is the past participle of eat, meaning consumed or swallowed up.

clue.text: Outstanding to keep good one taken inside

indicators.note: taken inside means the numeral goes within the other word

parts.note: to own something is to keep it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something exceptional kept the good one indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still to be paid, so the money is still due.

clue.text: Basically mean to keep empty house

indicators.note: to keep means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it

indicators.note: empty says only the outer letters of the word remain, the inside cleared out

explanation.surface: Essentially stingy, wanting to hang onto an unoccupied home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy but is the verb to intend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for when all is said and done serves as an adverb meaning fundamentally.

clue.text: Power and energy beginning to affect plant

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Power and energy start to influence a plant's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden pea is a climbing leguminous plant.

clue.text: Minister upset salesperson over project

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to project is to stick out, to reach

explanation.surface: A government minister is disturbed when a sales rep takes over a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles REP and REACH together. 'Minister' suggests politics but means clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion preaches sermons, so a clergyman is a sermon-giver.

clue.text: Syndicate's backer opening show

indicators.note: the backer of a word is its back end, the final letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A syndicate's financial supporter is launching a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A show such as a sporting or social occasion is an organised event.

clue.text: Doctor favourite to avoid extremes she's inspiring

indicators.note: to avoid extremes means the first and last letters of the combined pieces are dropped

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it
a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A GP's favourite patient keeps clear of anything excessive and inspires others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal but is the verb to neuter. The outer N and T of NEUTERPET go.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the Muse of music and lyric poetry, a source of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Discordant noise from drifted sand in port?

parts.note: a dune is a mound of drifted sand
a din is a loud discordant noise

explanation.surface: Harsh noise comes off sand blown into a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The noise comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin in New Zealand's South Island is a city with its harbour of Port Chalmers; the question mark flags the loose label.

clue.text: Everyone in rush to hide hotel soap

indicators.note: in means the word goes inside the other
to hide something is to put it out of sight, so this letter vanishes

parts.note: to rush is to dash
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everyone races to conceal a bar of soap at the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running US television soap opera set among Texas oil barons.

clue.text: Jacket ready for Putin in twice as much hot water?

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket of Tudor times
ready means cash, and Putin's Russian cash is in roubles

explanation.surface: A garment and some cash for the Russian president, who is in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for money; the Russian currency is the rouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot water is idiom for difficulty, so twice as much of it is twofold difficulty.

clue.text: Sibling success after Latin edict rubbished

indicators.note: after places the win behind the rearranged words
rubbished means trashed, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a win is a success

explanation.surface: Victory comes after an ancient Roman decree is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbished' turns LATIN EDICT into IDENTICAL T, and WIN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister from one fertilised egg, so genetically the same, is a kind of sibling.

clue.text: Mounted team that collects live goats

definitions.note: the singular form also serves as the plural

indicators.note: that collects means the first piece gathers the second inside it
mounted in a down clue means raised up, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
to live is to be

explanation.surface: A cavalry squad that rounds up living goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild mountain goat of the Alps, with long curved horns, is an example of goats.

clue.text: See 24
Hitch where corporation invests hospital billions

indicators.note: invests means the first word is clothed around the second

parts.note: corporation is old jocular slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A snag, as a big company puts billions into a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' means a pot belly here, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch a lift is to thumb one, signalling with a raised digit.

clue.text: Perhaps one's 3, 10, 12, 23, or 24A 25 — 13 down certainly

parts.note: every one of the listed solutions is a replica of a person's physical self, and a cloned creature is exactly that

explanation.walkthrough: The listed answers are a dead ringer, an image, a facsimile, a double and an identical twin: each copies a body, and a clone does so literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike duplicating someone's physical form is a reproduction of their frame.

clue.text: Boredom seen in pupil regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Tedium is observed in a schoolchild every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness from lack of interest, a French loanword.

clue.text: Protected as Crown Land spoilt with melee?

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Royal estate damaged in a brawl, now under protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royal property but means a tooth's crown, coated in enamel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth's crown is coated with hard glaze, so it is shielded in that way.
